# names a fn bound for a named param as the interpreter's frame binding
# does (nameFrameFns). These were frontier-hof-audit.tsv rows 74, 96, 135
# and 136, each a ledgered "body result of unknown provenance" refusal.

# increment): `apply` over a Dynamic value inside a fn unit records as an
# apply event (OpCallDynApplyOne — one result or a defer), and a value that
# is no fn at run time raises the interpreter's own apply no-match, natively
# and byte for byte. This was frontier-hof-audit.tsv row 194, the negative
# twin of the "apply over a dynamic lead" pair; its positive twin compiles
# too but islands (the map-member lambda is not stamped) and stays in the
# frontier corpus, ledgered as "islanded". The plain check flags this row's
# no-match at the call over the concrete rule map (diagnostic_parity_test.go).

column1: # apply over a PRODUCED closure at the main program GRADUATED 2026-09-08
# (the twenty-eighth increment): the `apply` word over a closure a factory
# call's unit returns registers a PENDING application, the check engine's
# re-step records it as the fn-value apply over the closure's producer
# operand (OpCallDynApplyTop — the runtime payload carries the captures),
# and a pending application no dispatch consumed refuses at Finalize. These
# were frontier-hof-audit.tsv rows 29, 30, 33, 34, 35 and 43 (§1 the
# classical bases I = S K K, C, K and W; §2 Church true), each ledgered as
# "computed closure at a word's argument slot"; every one runs VM-native.
def kk x:Any => [y:Any => [x/v]] end def ss f:Function => [g:Function => [x:Any => [(x g/v apply) (x f/v apply) apply]]] end def ii (kk/v (ss kk/v) apply) end 42 ii/v apply

column1: # the apply op's native entry under the APPLIED VALUE's contract, same
# increment: the event form (OpCallDynApplyOne) entered a stamped fn-value
# unit only when the UNIT declared the one return the model committed, and a
# stamped lambda unit declares none of its own — so every const lambda the
# apply word met, stamped and ready, ran on the interpreter island instead.
# The entry now reads the applied value's contract (the one the frame's RET
# enforces). Church FALSE (row 44) — its capture-free inner lambda is a
# stamped const — and the fetched-fn apply's positive twin (row 187, the
# twenty-seventh increment's "islanded" row) run native.
def cfalse t:Any => [f:Any => [f/v]] end def cif p:Function => [t:Any => [e:Any => [e/v (t/v p/v apply) apply]]] end 'F' ('T' (cif cfalse/v) apply) apply

# check pass's call-site residual now collapses the window the same way
# (EmitRecorder.UnitTailApply → collapseTailApply), so the produced-closure
# apply records instead of refusing the capture. These were
# frontier-hof-audit.tsv's two §1 B rows (audit §5.8 over B; the NUR089
# call-site pair).

column1: # a produced closure at a DECLARED Function slot GRADUATED 2026-09-08 (the
# thirtieth increment): a closure a factory call returns, handed to a user
# fn's `p:Function` param, is the call's argument (the interpreter's frame
# binding installs it as data), so the argument-slot hold no longer refuses
# it. Lifting the hold exposed a latent memo-key collision — a lambda body
# that is one `=>` group carries no position, and two such lambdas of one
# shape shared one compiled unit (cif's returned closure ran cnot's body,
# T for F) — fixed by keying such a body on its canonical text. These were
# frontier-hof-audit.tsv's two §2 `cnot` rows (Church not true / not false).

def ctrue t:Any => [f:Any => [t/v]] end def cfalse t:Any => [f:Any => [f/v]] end def cif p:Function => [t:Any => [e:Any => [e/v (t/v p/v apply) apply]]] end def cnot p:Function => [t:Any => [f:Any => [t/v (f/v p/v apply) apply]]] end 'F' ('T' (cif (cnot ctrue/v)) apply) apply

def ctrue t:Any => [f:Any => [t/v]] end def cfalse t:Any => [f:Any => [f/v]] end def cif p:Function => [t:Any => [e:Any => [e/v (t/v p/v apply) apply]]] end def cnot p:Function => [t:Any => [f:Any => [t/v (f/v p/v apply) apply]]] end 'F' ('T' (cif (cnot cfalse/v)) apply) apply
# the Church pair rows GRADUATED 2026-09-08 (the thirty-first increment): inside
# the projection's unit a lambda VALUE beneath the fn-typed param's pending
# tail apply is the apply's ARGUMENT (applyHandler re-steps the fn over the
# resolved stack, where a parked lambda is data the pair's Function param
# binds), so the unit finish's whole-residual window takes it; and at the main
# program the `/v` read of a def-bound produced closure — a fresh wrap of the
# binding with no provenance of its own — is traced to the bind's producer by
# name while the binding is still the bind's. These were frontier-hof-audit.tsv's
# two §5.8 Church pair rows (first and second projection).
def cpair a:Any => [b:Any => [s:Function => [b/v (a/v s/v apply) apply]]] end def cfst p:Function => [(a:Any => [b:Any => [a/v]]) p/v apply] end def p (2 (cpair 1) apply) end (cfst p/v)
def cpair a:Any => [b:Any => [s:Function => [b/v (a/v s/v apply) apply]]] end def csnd p:Function => [(a:Any => [b:Any => [b/v]]) p/v apply] end def p (2 (cpair 1) apply) end (csnd p/v)
# the Church and/or rows GRADUATED 2026-09-08 (the thirty-second increment): a fn
# VALUE beneath the `apply` word is data — applyHandler re-steps the applied fn
# over the resolved stack, where a fn value never dispatches — so the paren-
# bounded pending apply admits a fn-typed entry in its window (`(q/v p/v apply)`
# hands q to p) and the gradual-lead event admits a fn-valued receiver
# (`cfalse/v (…) apply` hands cfalse to the applied closure). These were
# frontier-hof-audit.tsv's §2 rows Church and (T and T) and Church or (F or F);
# their twins (T and F, T or F) compile and agree but still island — a def'd
# lambda's value applied inside a unit through a carrier lead — and stay
# ledgered as islanded.

def ctrue t:Any => [f:Any => [t/v]] end def cfalse t:Any => [f:Any => [f/v]] end def cif p:Function => [t:Any => [e:Any => [e/v (t/v p/v apply) apply]]] end def cand p:Function => [q:Function => [cfalse/v (q/v p/v apply) apply]] end 'F' ('T' (cif (ctrue/v (cand ctrue/v) apply)) apply) apply

def ctrue t:Any => [f:Any => [t/v]] end def cfalse t:Any => [f:Any => [f/v]] end def cif p:Function => [t:Any => [e:Any => [e/v (t/v p/v apply) apply]]] end def cor p:Function => [q:Function => [q/v (ctrue/v p/v apply) apply]] end 'F' ('T' (cif (cfalse/v (cor cfalse/v) apply)) apply) apply
# the U combinator GRADUATED 2026-09-08 (the thirty-second increment, found by
# the frontier gate): `(s/v s/v apply)` puts a fn value beneath the apply word —
# data on the resolved stack — so the self-application compiles; the factorial
# agrees on both lanes and runs VM-native. This was frontier-hof-audit.tsv's §4
# row (audit §1.4).
def fgen fn s:Function Function [ ( fn n:Integer Integer [ if (lte 1 n) [1] [ mul n ((sub 1 n) (s/v s/v apply) apply) ] ] ) ] end def fact (fgen fgen/v) end (fact 5)
# the CPS rows GRADUATED 2026-09-08 (the thirty-fourth increment): a pending
# `apply`-word application at a branch ARM's tail (`[ 1 k/v apply ]`, a fn-typed
# param applied inside the arm with its window inside the arm) collapses to the
# one gradual value the apply nets, recorded as the apply event in the arm's
# fragment (the arm frame seals the enclosing stack off on both lanes); the
# thirty-third increment resolved the fn-local capturing literal's `/v` read
# (`kk/v`) these rows hand to the recursive call. These were
# frontier-hof-audit.tsv's two §3 rows (audit §1.3, continuation-passing style).
def factk fn [[n:Integer k:Function][Any][ if (lte 1 n) [ 1 k/v apply ] [ def kk ( fn r:Integer Any [ def m (mul n r) m k/v apply ] ) (factk (sub 1 n) kk/v) ] ]] end (factk 5 (v:Integer => [v]))
